nextpyp.description: nextPYP (Bartesaghi lab, Duke University) is a web application for single-particle cryo-EM and cryo-electron tomography: pre-processing, particle picking, sub-tomogram averaging, constrained refinement and classification, run as projects in a browser. https://nextpyp.app nextPYP runs as two Apptainer images. This container includes the web server image (`nextPYP.sif`) and the `nextpyp` launcher. The processing image (`pyp.sif`, about 43 GB) is too large to include, so `nextpyp install` downloads it once into a directory you choose. The web server then runs from that directory in a nested Apptainer container. ### Install once Pick a writable directory with at least 50 GB free plus room for your projects (raw movies and tilt series need several TB). Every parent directory must be group- and world-executable (`chmod go+x`), which nextPYP enforces, so use project or scratch storage rather than a private home directory.

smartscope.description: SmartScope (NIEHS and Duke University) screens cryo-EM grids automatically. It drives the microscope through SerialEM: it acquires an atlas, finds and ranks squares and holes, collects high-magnification images and reports CTF and ice-thickness estimates in a web interface. https://smartscope.org Upstream ships SmartScope as several docker-compose services. This container runs them all from one image: MariaDB, Redis, the SmartScope web application (gunicorn behind nginx) and its Celery worker. It also includes IMOD 5.1.13 (`alignframes`) and CTFFIND 5.0.2, which SmartScope uses to process high-magnification movies. ### Create an instance once An instance directory holds the database, settings, logs and screening data. Choose a writable directory that keeps the same path in later sessions. The container image itself is read-only.
